% RETURN, REBASED · EOD 2026-09-21
CYCLICALS LEADCyclicals +3.7% vs defensives on the month
Rotation ReadCitrini · claude

Energy is the only cyclical sector still standing, and everything else in the leadership book is defensive or secular. XLE leads with +2.32% over the month and +40.26% year to date, while XLI lags at -9.45% and sits at just +6.79% for the year. XLU, the purest defensive utility trade, is down -6.47%, and XLRE is off -4.51%. So the money is not rotating into safety, it is rotating into the one corner of the cyclical complex that still has a commodity tailwind and into secular growth stories that ignore the economic cycle.

The theme table makes that split unambiguous. Cyber at +10.0% and Software at +6.7% are the strongest baskets, with Cyber at +82.6% year to date. Gold miners add +3.5% and Energy adds +2.8%. On the other side, Quantum is down -19.5%, Uranium -12.9%, Semis -10.2%, Defense -10.0%, GLP-1 -8.3%, and Industrials -8.1%. This is a market paying up for recurring revenue and hard assets while dumping anything tied to capex cycles, government spending, or speculative technology. The tension is that credit is not confirming the risk-off move. HYG/IEF sits at a z-score of 2.38, in the top 100% of its 1-year range, and BKLN/HYG is at 2.52. Credit spreads are tight and getting tighter, which means the bond market sees no recession. Equity rotation is defensive while credit is pricing expansion. One of them is wrong, and the credit ratios are the ones you should trust until they break.

The most stretched relative-strength readings tell you where positioning is crowded. XLE/XLU at a z of 2.35, in the top 100% of its range and +46.57% year to date, is the single most extended cyclical-vs-defensive bet on the board. USO/GLD at 2.05 and +130.24% year to date confirms the energy-over-gold trade is stretched. GDXJ/GDX at -2.08 sits in the bottom 1% of its range, meaning small gold miners have collapsed relative to large ones. XLY/SPY at -2.06, XLU/SPY at -2.05, and XLRE/SPY at -2.02 are all in the bottom 1% of their yearly ranges. IWB/SPY at -1.95 is in the top 7%, which tells you equal weight is losing to cap weight and the broad market is narrowing, not broadening.

Credit is priced for expansion while equity sector rotation is priced for slowdown.

BULL

High yield versus Treasuries at a z of 2.38 and loans versus high yield at 2.52 show the bond market has zero recession fear, and Cyber at +10.0% and Energy at +2.8% are still working as risk positions.

BEAR

XLI at -9.45%, XLU at -6.47%, and XLRE at -4.51% over the month show the cyclical and rate-sensitive equity complex is breaking down, and Defense at -10.0% and Semis at -10.2% confirm the capex cycle is being sold.

TELL

Watch HYG/IEF at its z of 2.38 and XLE/XLU at 2.35. If the credit ratio rolls while energy holds, the equity slowdown is the true signal. If energy breaks and credit stays tight, buy the cyclical dip.

⚠ High yield credit spreads are at their tightest of the year, with HYG/IEF at a z of **2.38** and in the top **100%** of its range. vs Defensive and rate-sensitive equity sectors are being sold hard, with XLU at **-6.47%** and XLRE at **-4.51%** over the month.: Credit says expansion while utilities and real estate say slowdown. Trust credit for now because the bond market leads equity sector rotation, but if HYG/IEF starts falling the equity read takes over.
⚠ Energy leads on both sector and theme performance, with XLE at **+2.32%** and the energy basket at **+2.8%** over the month. vs XLE/XLU is the most stretched cyclical ratio at a z of **2.35**, in the top **100%** of its 1-year range.: Energy leadership is trend-confirmed, not a reversion setup. Trust the trend, but size smaller because the ratio is extended and any oil pullback hits the crowded side.

The credit and cyclical ratios are trend-confirmed, not mean-reversion candidates. BKLN/HYG at 2.52 and HYG/IEF at 2.38 are both in the top 100% of their 1-year ranges and have been trending higher all year, with HYG/IEF up +2.94%.

XLE/XLU at 2.35 and +46.57% year to date is the most extended cyclical bet on the board, and USO/GLD at 2.05 and +130.24% year to date is the most extreme commodity ratio in the set. Do not fade these.

The genuine mean-reversion candidates are the longs that have been crushed into the bottom of their ranges. GDXJ/GDX at -2.08, in the bottom 1% of its yearly range, XLY/SPY at -2.06 and the bottom 0%, XLU/SPY at -2.05 and the bottom 1%, and XLRE/SPY at -2.02 and the bottom 1% are all stretched to the downside.

Those are the ratios where a bounce is more likely than another leg lower, unless the credit ratios confirm the slowdown by rolling over first.
